p4u1_protocol_v0_2_2026-09-23: Follow-up to p4u1_protocol_2026-09-23 (same day), requested by the project owner after a thorough methodological review of the v0.1 protocol -- still no code written. Three points identified as genuinely blocking before implementation: (1) the negative/null model ('same topology') was not precisely defined -- preserving exact topology risks preserving exactly the paths the null model must destroy; (2) no multiple-comparisons correction was planned -- with potentially thousands of candidate skeletons from discover_paths(), at least one is expected to look exceptional by pure chance even if each is individually improbable under noise, making false positives near-guaranteed without correction; (3) Gate B/C remained qualitative ('pre-registered threshold', 'must remain observable') rather than explicit scores and thresholds. New documentation/P4U1_Unsupervised_Compositional_Pattern_Discovery_V0_2.md fully supersedes v0.1 (kept as historical record of the review, marked non-implementable as-is). Fixes: (1) a label-stratified configuration-model null (degree-and-label-preserving graph randomization, a standard network-science technique, not invented ad hoc), N_null=200 replicates by default (matching the 200-500 Monte Carlo trial scale already used in m6_internal_regularized_diagnosis_v0_1.py), seeded deterministically; (2) a max-statistic (Westfall-Young-style) family-wise correction -- for each null replicate, take the MAXIMUM support across ALL candidate skeletons, build a null distribution of these per-replicate maxima, and compare the observed candidate against that distribution's 99th percentile, never a candidate-by-candidate null comparison; (3) Gate B and Gate C become fully quantitative and symmetric (support >= absolute minimum AND > null-max percentile AND depth >= min_depth, evaluated identically on train for Gate B and on holdout for Gate C using holdout's own separately-generated null replicates). Also incorporates: min_depth=2/max_depth=3 imposed explicitly (a length-1 edge is not a composition); U1 now includes real-motif competition against 3 named decoys (train-only, sub-threshold, depth-1) so the case tests DISCOVER+SELECT, not just SEARCH+MATCH; U1/U2/U3 redefined so the null-model replicates are a cross-cutting statistical control generated per-case, never a fourth dataset type; a pre-registered, purely structural (never target-dependent) rule for choosing which holdout nodes are valid replay starts, with a coverage metric (fraction of admissible starts producing the pattern); FrozenPattern gains a structural_digest field, built the exact same way as p4t_structural_transformation_induction_v0_1.freeze()'s own structural_digest (sha256 of only the anonymized structural fields, confirmed by direct reading of that function), invariant to training node/path identity and observation ordering; max_paths determinism (identical limit across train and all null replicates, never asymmetric); a formal witness schema per case (expected Gate A/B/C outcome and rejection reason per named candidate); and a naming discipline (always 'Unsupervised COMPOSITIONAL PATTERN Discovery', never shortened, to prevent future status inflation after a positive result). A 12-item pre-registration checklist is specified, distinguishing what this v0.2 already fixes in FORM (null model, correction method, gate structure, digest, start rule, witness schema) from what remains to be fixed as NUMBERS only when the real locked benchmark is built (N_null exact value, S_min, K_min, percentile thresholds, coverage threshold) -- and explicitly before ever running the benchmark, never after seeing a holdout result. No code, no locked cases, no tests exist yet for P4-U.1 -- this remains a protocol-only step. 704 tests collected, unchanged (694 passed + 10 deselected live-network demos) -- documentation-only change. See documentation/P4U1_Unsupervised_Compositional_Pattern_Discovery_V0_2.md for the full v0.2 protocol.

p4u2_calibration_experiment_2026-09-23: P4-U.2 disposable calibration experiment (2026-09-23), executed following the project owner's explicit direction that read P4U2_Protocol_V0_1.md (commit f6a96b2) and identified three prioritized scientific locks to resolve before any implementation: which cohesion statistic to use, which null model strategy to use, and a first quantitative proposal for Gate H's contradiction tolerance. Full report: documentation/P4U2_Calibration_Experiment_2026-09-23.md. Execution script was disposable and NOT committed (same discipline as P4-U.1's own scripts/_scratch_p4u1_calibration.py, not committed), run from the session scratchpad; only the report and its findings are preserved in the repository. Reused the unchanged multi-depth structural signature from the identifiability experiment (depth1/depth2/depth3 path counts filtered to paths whose first step is the edge itself, plus the set of observed direction sequences), computed via kernel2.discover_paths() unmodified. Three candidate cohesion statistics were tested rather than chosen a priori: Cohesion_A (proportion of common binarized structural traits), Cohesion_B (mean intra-group signature distance converted to a cohesion score), and Cohesion_C (frequency of the single most common full signature class within the group -- deliberately the same logic the identifiability experiment proved unsafe when used in ISOLATION, retested here specifically against a null model to see whether that rescues it). Three null model variants were tested: topology-only (rewire the whole graph's source/target assignment globally, no per-label stratification possible since P4-U.2 masks operators individually, unlike P4-U.1), group-resample-only (keep the real observed topology fixed, resample which edges form the candidate group), and combined (both). Four synthetic corpora, N_null=200 per variant: SEP (clear signal, 20 real edges with a guaranteed depth-2 continuation among 40 decoy/continuation edges), TWIN (4 disjoint directed 20-cycles, 80 edges, EVERY edge has a strictly identical signature by construction -- a genuinely homogeneous population where no subset should be distinguishable from any other), PARTIAL (exact structural reproduction of the identifiability experiment's Corpus 3, an 80%/20% noisy-but-real signal), and PURE_NULL (5 independent repeats, fully random graph, false-positive rate gauge). DECISIVE finding on the null model, empirically demonstrated rather than argued: on Corpus TWIN, group-resample-only correctly returns z=0.0 exactly (all three cohesion statistics) -- the correct 'no distinction' answer for a rigorously homogeneous population -- while topology-only (and combined, which inherits the same flaw) falsely declares massive significance (z up to 31.7), because rewiring the whole graph's topology destroys the entire corpus's global regularity, not just the candidate group's, answering a different question than the one Gate I must decide. Direct conclusion: Gate I's primary null model must be built around group-membership resampling on the fixed observed topology, never around whole-graph topology rewiring alone. On the cohesion statistic question, no single winner emerged: all three detect Corpus SEP's clear signal unambiguously, but on Corpus PARTIAL (the hard, noisy case) under the validated group-resample null model, all three land at the same borderline level (percentile 93.8, z between 1.62 and 1.87), just under the conventional 95%/z=1.96 significance threshold -- an honest measurement of limited statistical power at this sample size (group of 20, N_null=200), not a calibration failure, and explicitly not yet resolved by choosing one statistic over another. The Gate H contradiction_support pilot behaved exactly as expected (linear: 0%, 5%, 15%, 30% of group members replaced by contradicting decoys produced contradiction_support = 0.000/0.050/0.150/0.300 exactly), with a provisional tolerance range of 0.10-0.15 proposed but explicitly not decided by this single pilot. Two methodology bugs were found and corrected BEFORE drawing any conclusion, continuing the project's established self-correction discipline: (1) an initial TWIN corpus construction mixed two genuinely different edge roles (continuing vs terminal) in its resampling pool, silently re-testing the same kind of signal as Corpus SEP rather than providing a genuine null case -- fixed by rebuilding TWIN as rigorously homogeneous directed cycles; (2) a '<=' percentile convention saturated at 100% on a perfectly degenerate null case (TWIN's group-resample result, where the true z-score was exactly 0.0), corrected by switching to a standard mid-rank percentile convention used throughout. Explicitly NOT tested in this pass: the multiple-comparisons correction (protocol Sec. 13 item 6) -- this calibration evaluated only one candidate group at a time, never the realistic multi-candidate scenario that will need a max-statistic correction directly analogous to P4-U.1's own; this remains entirely open. Full report: documentation/P4U2_Calibration_Campaign2_2026-09-24.md. Execution script disposable, NOT committed, run from the session scratchpad, reusing every helper from campaign 1's own script unmodified (structural signature, three cohesion statistics, group-resample-only null model); topology-only was not retested since campaign 1 already eliminated it decisively. Four parts. Part 1+2A (signal-strength sweep, group_size=20, N_null=300, p_group from 0.5 to 1.0 on a generalized graded corpus subsuming SEP and PARTIAL as special cases): all three cohesion statistics show strictly monotone z-score growth with signal strength, crossing the conventional 95%/z=1.96 threshold between p_group=0.8 and 0.9 -- meaning campaign 1's PARTIAL case (80/20) sits almost exactly at the natural detectability boundary for this sample size. Part 2B (sample-size sweep, p_group=0.8 fixed, group_size from 10 to 80): power increases sharply and monotonically with sample size alone -- at group_size=40 the same 80/20 signal already clears the threshold comfortably for all three statistics, directly showing the borderline result is a SAMPLE-SIZE effect, not a broken statistic. Part 2C (N_null sweep from 200 to 2000, signal and size fixed): percentile/z remain stable across this range, ruling out an under-sampled null model as an explanation. Combined conclusion, demonstrated rather than assumed: the PARTIAL case's borderline result in campaign 1 is caused by insufficient sample size, not by an insufficient cohesion statistic and not by an overly conservative null model. Part 3 (multiple-comparisons correction, tested for the first time rather than assumed): a corpus with 1 true signal group (90% continuation) plus 9 null candidate groups drawn from an unstructured random background pool. A family-wise max-statistic null (P4-U.1's own discipline, here tested directly: for each replicate, draw as many independent random subsets as candidates under test and record the maximum statistic value, then use its 95th percentile as a single shared threshold) gives 0/9 false positives for all three cohesion statistics while still correctly detecting the true signal group. Without correction (each candidate judged against its own individual null), Cohesion_A alone lets 3 of the 9 signal-free candidates falsely pass (a 33% false discovery rate on this run) -- a concrete, demonstrated risk eliminated only by the correction. Caveat disclosed explicitly: single random seed, not yet a multi-seed calibrated false-positive/true-positive rate. Part 4 (Gate H contradiction_support, finer sweep from 0% to 50% in 5-point steps): confirms the strict linearity already seen in campaign 1 at finer resolution, but explicitly does NOT resolve the project owner's actual request -- determining separately the ACCEPT boundary (a genuinely coherent group under natural measurement noise) and the REJECT boundary (a manifestly heterogeneous group) requires a differently-designed corpus producing natural noise rather than discrete controlled replacement along a single dimension; left explicitly open, not claimed as resolved. Still no single cohesion statistic is chosen; Cohesion_A's demonstrated vulnerability without correction is noted as an argument for never skipping the multiple-comparisons correction regardless of which statistic is eventually chosen.
